 Key points
 The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare has reiterated the family pension priority order for central government staff, the memorandum said. 
 A spouse, including one married after retirement, is considered first for family pension. 
 Children qualify next, followed by dependent parents, with the mother ordinarily ahead of the father. 
 In marital discord, a woman employee or pensioner may nominate her children ahead of her husband; after a judicial separation, children are paid before the separated spouse. 
 A first-category child's family pension stops at 25, on marriage, or on starting to earn — whichever comes first. 
 Advertisement
 New Delhi, 10 November: A deceased central government employee’s or pensioner’s spouse is considered first for family pension under Rule 50 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, then children, and only then dependent parents, the pension department has said.
 The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare issued the instruction to ensure claims are examined the same way across government. “The following position is reiterated for uniform examination of claims,” the department said in the memorandum, dated 29 October.
 The spouse comes first, including an eligible post-retiral spouse — one married after the employee or pensioner had already retired — subject to conditions laid down in the rule, the memorandum said. Children become eligible only after the death of the spouse or when the spouse’s entitlement ends.
 Who comes after the spouse
 Children who count include adopted children, step-children, and children born after the employee or pensioner’s retirement or death, according to the memorandum. Among this first category, eligibility follows the order of birth — the eldest eligible child first.
 When a child’s share ends
 A first-category child’s family pension stops at the age of 25, on marriage, or on starting to earn a livelihood, whichever happens first, the memorandum said. Only when no child in that category is left eligible do children with a mental or physical disability become eligible, again in order of birth. A disabled child keeps the family pension until they start earning, and marriage does not end that eligibility.
 Daughters and dependent parents
 If no children in the first two categories are eligible, unmarried, widowed or divorced daughters become eligible next, in order of birth, provided they were dependent on the parent and are not earning when the pension becomes payable to them, the memorandum said. Their family pension runs until marriage, remarriage, or they start earning, whichever is earlier.
 Dependent parents, including adoptive parents, are considered only after both the spouse and the children’s eligibility has ended. Between the two parents, the memorandum says the mother ordinarily comes first.
 Last in line are dependent brothers and sisters with a mental or physical disability, who may get family pension only after the spouse, the children and the dependent parents are no longer eligible.
 When the spouse does not come first
 The memorandum lists two exceptions. In cases of marital discord, a woman government servant or pensioner may nominate her children to receive family pension ahead of her husband, if the prescribed conditions are met. And where a couple is judicially separated, eligible children are paid first; the separated spouse may be paid only after the children stop being eligible.
 It also notes that in the cases set out in Rule 50(8)(e) to (g), family pension may be paid to the surviving widow together with eligible children of another deceased wife, of a divorced wife, or from a void or voidable marriage.
 The instruction restates the existing rule rather than changing it, and tells ministries how Rule 50 is to be applied. Ministries and departments have been asked to bring it to the notice of officials dealing with family pension; it asks nothing of families. It goes to all ministries, departments and organisations of the Government of India, and covers families whose pension falls under the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 — not state government or EPS-95 families, whose rules are separate.
 The memorandum issues with the approval of the competent authority and is signed by Deepak Gupta, Under Secretary to the Government of India.
 The memorandum does not state how much family pension is paid. Readers can work out their own figures with our family pension calculator ; earlier reports cover family pension after a pensioner dies and how much a spouse gets .
 Source: Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare, O.M. No. 1/1(39)/2026-P&PW (E), 29 October 2026 — Order of priority among eligible family members for payment of family pension.

 Critical AdSense behaviour: adsbygoogle.push({}) does NOT bind to
 a specific . It says "process the next unbound in DOM
 order." So if you push N times, AdSense binds the first N 
 slots it finds.
 Live investigation (2026-05-29) showed the right sidebar still
 loading late on indianpaycalculator.in. DOM order of :
 1. LEFT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-left)
 2-5. Display banners (4× AdBanner inside page content)
 6. RIGHT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-right, after main slot)
 7. Mobile anchor (StickyAnchorAd at body end)
 Previously this script pushed twice (one per sidebar). Those 2
 pushes bound LEFT + Display#1, NOT LEFT + RIGHT. The other 5
 slots only got bound as AdBanner.client:visible islands hydrated
 on scroll — meaning the right sidebar was bound 6th, after the
 user scrolled past every in-page banner. That's the "right side
 opens very late" complaint.
 Fix: push once per SSR'd ad slot. AdSense binds them all in DOM
 order at body parse end — no React hydration wait, no scroll-to-

 StickyAnchorAd) become no-ops since the AdUnit effect skips when
